sections.content: How many people stayed in Mossley after gaining qualifications?

Mossley is a small town in the North West. Mossley does not have its own university.

Mossley has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Mossley ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 460 state-school pupils from Mossley who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 140 (30%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 160 (35%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Mossley to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Mossley's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Mossley in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Mossley move to?

Of Mossley's graduates, 50 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those graduates (50%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Mossley's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 55 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those qualified non-graduates (91%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Mossley's GCSE cohort:

  • 30 graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 43% of graduates and 44% of qualified non-graduates living in Mossley had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 150 graduates and 180 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Mossley. This is compared with the 140 graduates and 160 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 57% of the graduates had also lived in Mossley as GCSE pupils, while 43% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Mossley in 2018 to 2019, 56% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 44% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
